title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #5

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What can you use to draw and label a plant if you have a computer at school? (1 mark)
   A. A stopwatch
   B. A ruler only
   C. A calculator only
   D. A drawing app

2. Which of these is a sign of life in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Growing taller over time
   B. Making a loud noise
   C. Changing into a stone
   D. Walking to find water

3. A bat flies but has fur and feeds its babies milk. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A reptile
   B. A mammal
   C. A bird
   D. An insect

4. Which of these is a safe thing to do on a science walk? (1 mark)
   A. Pick up unknown snakes
   B. Tease insects
   C. Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   D. Throw stones at birds

5. Why is a plan for a healthy digestive system useful? (1 mark)
   A. It cures all diseases at once
   B. It stops us feeling hungry
   C. It reminds us to do the right things every day
   D. It makes us grow overnight

6. In the mouth, which part helps to move food around and swallow? (1 mark)
   A. Tongue
   B. Gullet
   C. Stomach
   D. Rectum

7. Which food group helps to prevent constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Sugary biscuits
   B. Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   C. Fizzy drinks
   D. Sweets

8. A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Sound
   C. Air only
   D. Matter

9. What happens to a gas that is put in a closed jar? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes a solid
   B. It spreads to fill the whole jar
   C. It sits at the top only
   D. It stays at the bottom

10. How many grams are in 5 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 500
   B. 50
   C. 50 000
   D. 5000

11. Why is polythene dangerous for goats and cows? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them sweet
   B. They may eat it and get sick
   C. It makes milk
   D. It makes them grow

12. What should never be done with waste in a place where children are playing? (1 mark)
   A. Put it in a bin
   B. Sort it
   C. Collect it
   D. Burn it

13. Why are rotting waste heaps a health danger? (1 mark)
   A. They cool the air
   B. They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   C. They make water sweet
   D. They make soil red

14. Which of these is needed to harvest rainwater from a roof? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. A gutter and a tank
   C. A fan
   D. A ladder only

15. Which of these describes recycling water? (1 mark)
   A. Letting water evaporate
   B. Wasting water
   C. Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   D. Boiling it and throwing it

16. Which of these is a result of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. More rain
   B. Less water for others
   C. Less money spent
   D. More trees

17. Why is a bucket better than a running tap for washing a bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the bicycle dirty
   B. It makes it heavier
   C. It uses more water
   D. It uses less water

18. When is the best time to water plants? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Noon
   C. Midday only
   D. Early morning or evening

19. Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house? (1 mark)
   A. Electric bulbs
   B. Sun through the door
   C. Moonlight
   D. Windows

20. A lighthouse is used to (1 mark)
   A. Warn ships of danger
   B. Cook food
   C. Grow plants
   D. Dry clothes

21. Which of these is a way of making a room lighter during the day? (1 mark)
   A. Closing the window
   B. Opening the curtains
   C. Painting the walls black
   D. Closing the door

22. Which of these artificial sources charges its battery in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Lightning
   B. Sun
   C. Solar lamp
   D. Stars

23. Why should candles and paraffin lamps be kept away from curtains? (1 mark)
   A. They can start a fire
   B. They make curtains dry
   C. They make curtains cold
   D. They make curtains bright

24. Which of these is transparent? (1 mark)
   A. Thick cardboard
   B. Clear glass
   C. Metal
   D. Wood

25. Why is a thermometer better than touching to find how hot something is? (1 mark)
   A. It is dangerous
   B. It is noisy
   C. It is safe and gives a number
   D. It is heavy

26. What should you do first if you burn your skin? (1 mark)
   A. Put butter on it
   B. Ignore it
   C. Cover it with soil
   D. Put it under cool running water and tell an adult

27. Why should kitchen gloves be dry? (1 mark)
   A. Dry cloth is heavier
   B. Dry cloth is colder
   C. Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   D. Wet cloth is thicker

28. Which is a correct statement about heat? (1 mark)
   A. It has mass
   B. It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   C. It moves from cold to warm
   D. It stays still

29. Why do wet clothes dry faster in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. The sun makes them heavy
   B. The sun makes water colder
   C. The sun adds water
   D. The heat evaporates the water

30. Why does hot tea cool down? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes heavier
   B. It gains light
   C. It loses heat to the air and cup
   D. It gains cold

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A school tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much water is lost in a school day of 8 hours and in 5 school days? (3 marks)

32. Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials. (2 marks)

33. Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials. (3 marks)

34. Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider. (5 marks)

35. Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day. (4 marks)

36. Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods. (5 marks)

37. Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun. (3 marks)

38. Give three problems caused by friction. (3 marks)

39. Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment. (5 marks)

40. State three ways of keeping teeth healthy. (3 marks)

41. Draw a simple diagram of the digestive system and label mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and anus. (5 marks)

42. Explain the difference between heat and temperature. (4 marks)

43. Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A drawing app
   A drawing app can be used to draw and label plant parts.

2. A — Growing taller over time
   Plants grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond and die. They do not walk or make noise.

3. B — A mammal
   The fur and milk feeding make it a mammal.

4. C — Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   Handling animals safely and washing hands avoids injury and germs.

5. C — It reminds us to do the right things every day
   A plan helps us follow healthy habits.

6. A — Tongue
   The tongue moves food and helps swallowing.

7. B — Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

8. D — Matter
   Mass is the amount of matter.

9. B — It spreads to fill the whole jar
   A gas fills any container it is in.

10. D — 5000
   5 x 1000 = 5000 g.

11. B — They may eat it and get sick
   Animals that eat polythene can become ill or die.

12. D — Burn it
   Burning near children is dangerous.

13. B — They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   Flies and rats carry germs.

14. B — A gutter and a tank
   Gutters carry rain to a tank.

15. C — Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   Recycling cleans water for another use.

16. B — Less water for others
   Wasted water is not available to others.

17. D — It uses less water
   A bucket has a limited amount of water.

18. D — Early morning or evening
   Less water evaporates when it is cooler.

19. A — Electric bulbs
   Bulbs are artificial light.

20. A — Warn ships of danger
   Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

21. B — Opening the curtains
   Open curtains let in more daylight.

22. C — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp is made by people.

23. A — They can start a fire
   Flames can set cloth on fire.

24. B — Clear glass
   Clear glass lets light through.

25. C — It is safe and gives a number
   A thermometer avoids burns and measures.

26. D — Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   Cool water reduces the burn.

27. C — Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   Wet cloth can burn your hand.

28. B — It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

29. D — The heat evaporates the water
   Heat makes water turn to vapour.

30. C — It loses heat to the air and cup
   Heat goes from the tea to the cooler surroundings.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 16 litres in one day and 80 litres in five days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 x 8, 1 mark for 16, 1 mark for 16 x 5 = 80.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It wears away shoes and tyres, wastes energy, makes machines hot and slows moving parts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brush at least twice a day, limit sweets and sugary drinks, visit a dentist, use clean toothbrush or chewing stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: A neat tube drawn from mouth to anus with each part labelled in the correct order.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for each of four correct labels.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat is energy that makes things hot. Temperature is how hot something is and it is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for heat and 2 marks for temperature.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.
